title: Light 3-stars in plane graphs of minimum face size five (Madaras)
abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of Theorem 1.1 of Madaras (2004), for finite simple graphs with the combinatorial planarity (genus-zero rotation systems) of the registered entry Kuratowski's theorem. In every plane map of a finite simple graph of minimum degree at least three whose faces all have length at least five, some vertex x of degree three has three distinct neighbours a, b, c with deg a = deg b = 3 and deg c ≤ 4 (light_star3); in particular the star K1,3 is light, with degree sum at most 13. One statement. The proof is a discharging argument on the rotation system with charges deg − 4 and ℓ − 4 in which every face gives each corner at a 3-vertex a weight depending only on the degrees of the two neighbours along the face, and vertices of degree at least five give 1/5 to each 3-neighbour; the local inequalities are checked by decide in the kernel. This replaces the article's transfer of charge between adjacent 3-vertices.
